To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the calcium-perme-able cation channel, CD20, is activated by IGF-I via the IGF receptor, and the activation requires GTP, Mg, and ATP in the patch-clamp mode and the α subunits (especially α2) of the G proteins.
the CD20 ion channel is activated by insulin growth factor I via G proteins.
the CD20 cation channel is activated by the α subunits, but not the βγ subunits, of heterotrimer G proteins, and that the α subunit of the Gi2 protein is the major G protein that activates CD20.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the calcium-permeability cation channel, CD20, by insulin-like growth-factor-I via G proteins in Balb/c3T3 cells.
the activation of the calcium-permea ble cation channel CD 20 by a subunits of the Gi protein, which is expressed in Balbc 3T3 fibroblast.
the regulation of ion channels by heterotrimeric guanine nucleotide-binding proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CD20 cation channel, which is expressed in Balbc3T3 cells and activated by insulin-like-growth factor-I via the insulin-like-growth-factor-I receptor, is activated by the α subunits (α1 and α2) of the G protein, Gs.

the CD20 cation channel expressed in Balbc 3T3 fibroblasts is activated by the α subunits (Gi2 and Gi3) of the Gi family of heterotrimer G proteins, and the βγ subunits of G proteins do not play a role in the regulation of CD20.
the CD20 cation channel is regulated by the IGF-1 receptor via G-protein α subunits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CD20 is activated by the α subunits, but not by the βγ subunits, of the Gi proteins.
the CD20 channels are activated by G proteins in a manner similar to the activation of the G protein-activated potassium channel.
IGF-I activates the CD20 channel via the IGF-1 receptor and Gi2 α subunits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD20 ion channel is regulated by the IGF-1 receptor through the α subunits (Gi2) of heterotrimer G-proteins.
the CD20 is a calcium-permeable channel activated by G proteins.
CD20 is activated by Gi2 α subunits in the absence of β and γ subunits.
